messages:
jen li: FYI I'm seeing a pretty sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on several private clusters after the kernel-routing change rolled last night. numbers in thread.
marc gonzalez: hm, only private? hosted/dedicated look fine?
alok patel: I saw a small dip on dedicated but nothing dramatic. private went from ~78% to ~26% on average for the same traffic window.
jen li: correct. hosted stayed ~80%. dedicated mid-60s -> ~55%. private is the outlier.
rachel kim: do we have any diffs in the cache keying logic between deployments? config drift maybe (normalize settings, strip_trailing_ws, hash versions)?
jen li: I compared code paths — runtime->kernel routing change touched the prompt-normalization shim used by our fp16 optimized kernels. it introduced a new normalization that trims repeated whitespace and collapses unicode NFKC. Looks like private builds were still on the older kernel binary that expects the old normalization schema.
alok patel: so mismatch between key generation formats across kernel versions. private store still has keys written by old serializer but runtime now generates new keys -> miss.
jen li: exactly. sample logs:
```
CACHE_LOOKUP key=v1:sha256:7a3b... miss (expected v0:sha256:02f4...)
NORMALIZER version=2 -> collapsed whitespace
STORE s3://private-prefix-cache/ (minio gateway)
```
marc gonzalez: and hosted uses memcached in-region with-agent that did a rolling restart and got the new normalizer + backend migration at same time, so it rewrote keys in-place. dedicated had local nvme store and we patched it during the canary so writes were consistent. private was missed during rollout because the private control plane flagged it as unchanged.
rachel kim: nice explanation. any quick mitigation? revert normalization or add compatibility layer that checks both key versions?
jen li: short-term: add a key fallback lookup that tries both v2 and v1 key namespaces for X minutes. also enqueue a background rewriter to materialize v2 keys for existing v1 entries in the private buckets.
alok patel: agree. I'll open a small PR for the dual-lookup and a migration job. we should gate the fallback behind a feature flag per-deployment.
marc gonzalez: can infra run a low-rate migration first on one private region to sanity-check object-store throughput? rewriter might spike requests.
infra-bot: deployment event: rolling-kernel-route v2 applied to hosted and dedicated at 2026-03-17T22:11Z. private clusters excluded due to control plane drift. ticket=INF-4472
jen li: timeline: I'll add the fallback now so hits recover for user traffic. migration job queued to run as low-concurrency job tomorrow. postmortem follow-up to prevent control-plane mismatches.
rachel kim: for the long-term, we need an automated compatibility test: simulate key roundtrip normalized on all kernel permutations and verify idempotency. add to CI matrix.
alok patel: will add a perf test that measures hit-rate delta after kernel swaps. also capture per-deployment cache hit histograms in the console so we can catch these earlier.
marc gonzalez: thanks team. jen, assign the PR to me for quick review. tag infra when you schedule the migration window.
jen li: done. :thumbsup:
